subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support an opt-in Slack mode that receives user-authorized DM events and replies as the configured Slack user, and what security gate should make that safe?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses from bot/app operation into regular-user impersonation and would change documented Slack token semantics, so code inspection cannot safely choose the product/security policy.

options.title: Design explicit act-as-user mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an opt-in config or equivalent setup flow, updated docs, live Slack proof, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Slack bot-only for inbound identity
options.body: Close or reject the request after documenting that user tokens remain read/helper credentials and bot/app identity owns inbound DM routing and replies.

options.title: Defer to a separate Slack plugin experiment
options.body: Let a non-core Slack plugin prototype the identity model first, then revisit core only if a missing SDK/channel API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design explicit act-as-user mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an opt-in config or equivalent setup flow, updated docs, live Slack proof, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack identity/security changes and docs work make this the best available routing owner for the product/security choice.
